findings.title: TotalDocs reads the cache map with no lock while BuildIndex writes to it
findings.body: `TotalDocs` loops over `b.cache` (line 146) without taking `cacheMu`. Line 138 now writes the map under `cacheMu.Lock()`, but a lock only one side takes does not stop the race. This PR adds a new caller, `search.go:216`, and it runs right after `search.go:207` has started the `handleEvent` goroutine. `handleEvent` → `getOrCreateIndex` → `BuildIndex` can then write `b.cache[key]` while `TotalDocs` is iterating it. The Prometheus collector does the same thing on every scrape (`bleve_index_metrics.go:96`). Go stops the whole process with `concurrent map iteration and map write` when this happens. Fix: take `b.cacheMu.RLock()`/`RUnlock()` in `TotalDocs`.

findings.title: Init workers share one `err` variable (and `totalBatchesIndexed`), and now really run in parallel
findings.body: Each `group.Go` closure assigns the outer `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and returns it. `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) is also shared. Before this PR, `BuildIndex` held `cacheMu` for the whole build, so builds ran one at a time. With the lock moved to just the map write (bleve.go:137-139), `initWorkers` builds now overlap. That is a data race: one goroutine can overwrite `err` with nil before another goroutine's `return err` reads it. `group.Wait()` would then report success for a failed build, and startup goes on with an index missing and nothing logged. Use a local variable (`_, _, err := s.build(...)`) and an atomic counter, or count after `Wait`.

findings.title: Stop no longer blocks requests: the `initErr` assignments in Stop are dead
findings.body: Before this PR, every handler called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returns `s.initErr`, so once `Stop` had set `initErr` to "service is stopping"/"service is stopped", requests were refused. Now the only call to `Init` is in the constructor, and `once` makes later calls return the stored value. Nothing reads `initErr` after `Stop`. After `Stop` cancels the backend (`sql/backend.go:119-122`) and `s.ctx`, Create/Read/List/Watch keep running against the stopped backend. Either check a stopped flag in the handlers or remove the assignments, so `Stop` does not appear to do something it no longer does. I found no caller of `server.Stop` inside `pkg/storage/unified`, so today this only affects code that calls the concrete type.

findings.title: Eager Init runs on a background context that the caller cannot cancel
findings.body: `Init` (DB init and ping, the full search index build, the watcher) now runs inside `NewResourceServer` on `s.ctx`. That context comes from `context.Background()` (line 229). `sql.NewResourceServer` receives the dskit `start` ctx (`sql/service.go:113`), but it cannot pass it in, because `ResourceServerOptions` has no context. The in-process path (`client.go:101`) runs this during dependency wiring. As a result, a shutdown requested during startup cannot interrupt a long index build, which now blocks startup. Consider accepting a ctx, or building the index in the background with readiness reported through `IsHealthy`.

findings.title: Postgres coverage turned off without a root cause; is it related to the eager Init?
findings.body: The storage-server module test is now skipped on postgres ("Works locally"), with no tracking issue. This PR moves resource-DB init (`dbProvider.Init` plus `PingContext`) into `NewResourceServer`, which runs inside the storage server's `start` (`sql/service.go:113`). The test gives startup a fixed 500 ms (line 56) before it calls `/metrics`. Is the CI failure caused by this new startup work? If so, skipping the test hides a startup regression rather than an environment problem. Please link an issue or fix the wait (for example, poll until ready instead of sleeping).

contracts.action: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init eagerly (lifecycle Init, search index build, watcher)
contracts.equivalent_path: Before: every RPC handler called s.Init(ctx) lazily on its first request
contracts.before_after: Before: Init ran on the first request, with that request's ctx, and an Init error was returned to every request. After: Init runs once in the constructor with the background s.ctx, an error stops the constructor, and handlers no longer check anything
contracts.visible_effect: The storage server's start (and in-process DI) blocks until the DB is ready and the full index is built; an init failure becomes a startup error instead of per-request errors
contracts.failure_mode: An Init error is logged twice (server.go:260 and :314) and returned, so the service fails to start. The build cannot be cancelled by the caller's ctx. After Stop, initErr is no longer seen by requests

contracts.action: The search index is initialized before the server watcher/broadcaster
contracts.equivalent_path: searchSupport.init subscribes on its own to backend.WatchWriteEvents, not through the broadcaster
contracts.before_after: The broadcaster is now created after the index build. Since Init runs in the constructor, no Watch RPC can reach a nil broadcaster
contracts.visible_effect: None to the user, beyond the startup time
contracts.failure_mode: If search init fails, the watcher is never started and the constructor returns an error

contracts.action: New call to s.search.TotalDocs() in search init log
contracts.before_after: Neither caller takes a lock. TotalDocs ranges over b.cache with no lock, while BuildIndex writes it under cacheMu
contracts.visible_effect: A log line with the duration and the document count
contracts.failure_mode: A concurrent map iteration and write (handleEvent started at line 207 builds an index) stops the process

contracts.action: bleve BuildIndex holds cacheMu only for the map write, not for the whole build
contracts.before_after: Before: all builds ran one at a time under the write lock (GetIndex blocked during builds). After: builds run in parallel up to initWorkers
contracts.visible_effect: Faster startup indexing; Search no longer blocks on unrelated builds
contracts.failure_mode: Exposes the shared-err race in search.init's worker closures and the unlocked TotalDocs read

summary: The PR runs resource-server Init eagerly in the constructor, removes the per-request Init gates, and narrows the bleve cache lock so index builds can run in parallel. Two issues follow from that, rated fix. First, `TotalDocs` reads the cache map with no lock while builds write to it; the read is reachable from the new init log line and from the metrics scrape, and a collision stops the process. Second, the init workers share one `err` variable and now really run in parallel, so a failed build can be reported as success. Lesser points: Stop no longer stops requests, eager Init cannot be cancelled by the caller, and the postgres test is skipped without a root cause.
